newsitem.title: CHINA: Japan hopes for cooperation with China on markets.
newsitem.headline: Japan hopes for cooperation with China on markets.

text.p: Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka on Wednesday told Chinese counterpart Liu Zhongli that Tokyo wanted to coooperate with Beijing on stabilising international financial markets, Japanese officials said.

Tokyo would this year hold a meeting for Asian emerging nations and international organisations to promote financial market stability, Ministry of Finance officials in Beijing with Mitsuzuka told a news briefing.

Mitsuzuka, who is in China on a four-day visit, told Liu Japan wanted to cooperate with Beijing on financial market stability, said Kenji Aramaki, director of the development finance division at the ministry's International Finance Bureau.

Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara, who attended the meeting, had told the Chinese that Tokyo would this year hold the first meeting of Asian emerging nations and organisations such as the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.
Japan had suggested such a meeting at last weekend's summit of the G7 nations in Denver, Aramaki said.
"My impression was that the Chinese side was positive about the idea," Aramaki said.
Chinese officials had said they wanted to discuss attendance at the Tokyo meeting with the People's Bank of China, he said.
